title_en: Visions of the Future (20/20): From Elixirs to Gene Editing
note_en: 从未…过 is a strong, formal "never (once)": 人类对死亡的恐惧似乎从未改变过 "humanity's fear of death seems never to have changed." 未 is the written equivalent of 没, and 过 marks experience over the whole span of time, so the phrase covers every moment up to now, much like English "has never." In everyday speech you would hear 从来没…过 instead.

Xiao Le pointed at the two pictures and asked Grandpa why the last exhibit had circled back to the first one they'd seen.

sentences.en: Xiao Le said she remembered asking Grandpa at the first exhibit that day whether life would become meaningless if you could live forever, and Grandpa had said that was exactly the question the old legend wanted people to think about. Now, looking at a real DNA model, she wondered whether science could actually answer that question. Grandpa said, "An old legend can only raise the question; it has no way of really testing it. Science may truly let people live longer, but whether life still has meaning once they do is a question no technology, however powerful, can answer. You have to think it through for yourself."
